$comment: The facts the agent-facing docs state, in one place. scripts/agent-docs.mjs fills them into agents/src/ templates; the service's own facts test fails when one differs from its code. The API version is read from openapi/openapi.yaml, never written here. sdk_version, cli_tagline and sign_in are checked against the TypeScript SDK and CLI, and python_package against python/pyproject.toml, by typescript/test/unit/agent-facts.test.ts.
sign_in: a Flow account (flow.engineer: Google, GitHub or an email link)
cli_tagline: Telegram, iMessage and WhatsApp for AI agents.

trial.$comment: The free trial on Flow's shared senders that a sign-in at flow.engineer (or the Flow CLI's setup) starts, once per account: people per channel over all the account's apps and both modes; the next person is held, not refused.

sending.$comment: The send gate's defaults for dedicated senders; a sender's own limits (its `limits`) win. messages_per_second and burst: Telegram bots' pacing. new_contacts_*: conversations a sender may start, per channel (Telegram's are effectively unlimited). abuse: the signals that throttle a dedicated sender (iMessage lines have stricter ones of their own).

mcp.owner_rule: Adding the Flow MCP server to a developer's coding tools is the project owner's decision: suggest it and show them the command, but never add it to their config yourself.
mcp.runtime_rule: MCP is not a runtime dependency: the app you build talks to Flow through the REST API (or the TypeScript or Python SDK, which wrap it) for everything it does at runtime.

add.claude: claude mcp add --transport http flow https://api.flow.engineer/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY"
